name: tagline
value: Exact, one-use authorization for agent payments. Your intent, enforced onchain.

name: description
value:
Maqam Protocol makes an agent payment match exactly what its owner authorized. An agent proposes an invoice payment, Maqam checks the proposal, and the owner signs typed payment terms. A Solidity executor on Arc Testnet validates the owner, executor, recipient, token, amount, expiry, nonce, revocation epoch, and evidence commitment before transferring USDC. Changed recipients and amounts fail signature validation. Reusing a completed approval fails even when calling the contract directly and bypassing the application. Owners can revoke one approval or invalidate all older approvals.

The demo includes a real recorded model proposal on a synthetic invoice, a separate owner and executor, confirmed Arc Testnet USDC payments, recorded adversarial checks, and a receipt viewer that re-verifies the mined transaction against the live chain without requiring a wallet. The wallet interface supports exact allowance approval, EIP-712 signing, execution, signed-packet export/import and revocation.

This is a Continuity project extending my existing Maqam agent-governance library. The contracts, wallet interface, Arc integration, proof viewer, model adapter and tests are new ETHOnline work. It is an unaudited testnet prototype: the receipt proves authorization consistency, not invoice truth or AI correctness.

name: howItsMade
value:
The new EVM boundary is written in Solidity with OpenZeppelin EIP712, SignatureChecker (including ERC-1271), SafeERC20 and ReentrancyGuard. Owner-scoped nonces are consumed atomically with transferFrom; reverted transfers preserve the authorization. Epoch invalidation revokes outstanding signatures. The browser checks runtime bytecode, excluding compiler-reported immutable slots, before authorization.

A Vite/JavaScript frontend uses ethers 6 for wallet signing, transaction submission and live receipt verification. A Vercel function invokes the existing MIT-licensed maqam@0.3.3 package for proposal policy. A separate local OpenAI-compatible agent adapter produced the recorded synthetic-invoice proposal using Azure OpenAI; no owner key or execution tool was supplied to the model. The hosted UI clearly labels this recorded call rather than claiming a live hosted AI service.

Arc is the settlement layer, using its native USDC ERC20 interface at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000. Payment units use six decimals; executor gas uses the shared native balance at eighteen decimals. The scripted proof uses separate owner and executor test accounts and retains transaction hashes, signatures and rejection evidence. Fifteen automated tests cover tampering, replay, expiry, wrong executor/domain, cancellation, epoch revocation, rollback, ERC-1271 and reentrancy.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted research, implementation, tests, UI and documentation. The repository preserves the specification, model prompts, evidence and incremental commits, and explicitly separates pre-existing Maqam from new event work. Human hands-on testing and the human-narrated demo are tracked separately; automated fixture signing is not represented as a human UX test.
